raw_text:
Below is the full integrated 12‑week muscle‑gain program for your 26‑year‑old vegan recreational lifter. It combines the 4‑day upper/lower lifting plan, phased progression, the intensified Phase 3 (Weeks 9–11) with a Week 12 deload, integrated cardio schedule, one weekly cheat‑meal day, post‑workout meal ideas, and protein/powder and supplement guidance — all tuned to a plant‑only diet and a daily protein target of 150 g. Use the program as a template; adjust loads, exercise selection, and calories to client response.

Quick overview
- Duration: 12 weeks (3 phases of 4 weeks).
- Frequency: 4 gym sessions/week (Upper A, Lower A, Upper B, Lower B).
- Cardio: 1 HIIT/Tempo (weekly), 1–2 LISS sessions, 1 active recovery mobility session.
- Cheat meal: 1 planned cheat‑meal day/week (preferably rest/active day).
- Nutrition target: 150 g protein/day (plant sources + protein powder), modest calorie surplus (~+300 kcal/day baseline; adjust).
- Supplements: vegan protein powder (pea+rice or pea isolate recommended), creatine monohydrate 5 g/day, B12, vitamin D if needed, optional algae omega‑3.

Phase breakdown
- Phase 1 Weeks 1–4: Foundation — technique, baseline volume, moderate loads (RPE ~6–7).
- Phase 2 Weeks 5–8: Progressive overload — heavier compounds, mixed reps (RPE ~7–8).
- Phase 3 Weeks 9–11: Push intensity — heavier compounds, advanced intensity techniques, reduced accessory volume (RPE ~8–9).
- Week 12: Deload — volume ~40–60% and optional light testing only if appropriate.

General progression rules
- Increase load when prescribed reps completed with good form and ~1–2 RIR remaining. Typical increments: +2.5–5% upper body, +5–10% lower body.
- If reps cannot be hit 2 sessions in a row, reduce load 5% or adjust recovery/nutrition.
- Prioritize sleep (7–9 h), hydration, and protein distribution (25–40 g per meal across 4–5 meals).

Weekly structure and cardio placement (example week)
- Mon (Day 1): Upper A — heavy/moderate (lifting). Optional 10–12 min easy bike post session.
- Tue (Day 2): Lower A — heavy/moderate (lifting).
- Wed (Day 3): LISS 30–35 min brisk walk or easy bike + mobility (active recovery).
- Thu (Day 4): Upper B — lifting (can host HIIT post‑session if preferred and energy OK).
- Fri (Day 5): Lower B — lifting.
- Sat (Day 6): HIIT or Tempo session OR rest (depending on schedule). Cheat‑meal day often Saturday.
- Sun (Day 7): Rest or 20 min easy walk + mobility.

Phase 1 — Weeks 1–4: Foundation (moderate intensity, higher volume)
Goals: teach/solidify technique, accumulate volume, prepare for heavier loads.

Week 1 (example)
Day 1 — Upper A (Push)
- Warm up 8–10 min mobility.
- Barbell bench press: 4 x 8 (2:0:1) RPE 6–7
- Incline dumbbell press: 3 x 10
- Seated overhead press (DB/machine): 3 x 10
- Cable fly: 3 x 12
- Lateral raises: 3 x 15
- Triceps rope pushdown: 3 x 12
- Core: Pallof press 3 x 30s/side

Day 2 — Lower A (Quads/glutes)
- Warm up/goblet squat warm sets.
- Back squat: 4 x 8
- Romanian deadlift: 3 x 10
- Walking lunges: 3 x 12/leg
- Leg press: 3 x 12
- Leg extension: 3 x 12–15
- Calf raise: 4 x 12–15
- Core: Dead bug 3 x 12/side

Day 3 — LISS 30–35 min brisk walk or easy bike + mobility

Day 4 — Upper B (Pull)
- Pull‑ups or lat pulldown: 4 x 6–8
- Barbell or DB bent‑over row: 4 x 8
- Seated cable row: 3 x 10
- Face pulls: 3 x 15
- Hammer curls: 3 x 12
- EZ bar curl: 3 x 10
- Rear delt raises: 3 x 15

Day 5 — Lower B (Hamstrings/glutes)
- Deadlift (conventional/trap): 4 x 6–8 (moderate)
- Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 10/leg
- Single‑leg RDL: 3 x 10
- Hip thrust: 4 x 10–12
- Hamstring curl: 3 x 12–15
- Standing calf raise: 4 x 12–15
- Core: Plank 3 x 45–60s

Days 6–7 — Active rest / mobility / easy walk

Weeks 2–4 progression (foundation)
- Week 2: small load increase on compounds if Week 1 sets completed.
- Week 3: add 1 set to a lagging accessory per session.
- Week 4: slight intensity increase (shorter rests or heavier loads) then weekend active recovery.

Phase 2 — Weeks 5–8: Progressive overload
Goals: increase load on main lifts, slightly lower rep ranges on compounds, maintain accessory volume.

Week 5 (example)
Day 1 — Upper A
- Bench press: 5 x 5 (RPE 7–8)
- Incline DB press: 3 x 8–10
- Seated overhead press: 4 x 8
- Cable fly: 3 x 12
- Lateral raises superset front raises: 3 x 12/12
- Weighted dips: 3 x 8–10

Day 2 — Lower A
- Back squat: 5 x 5
- RDL: 4 x 8
- Walking lunges: 3 x 12/leg
- Leg press (heavy): 3 x 10
- Calf raise: 4 x 10–12
- Core: Hanging leg raise 3 x 10–12

Day 3 — LISS 25–35 min (or rest)

Day 4 — Upper B
- Weighted pull‑ups: 5 x 5–6
- Barbell row: 4 x 6–8
- 1‑arm DB row: 3 x 10
- Face pulls: 4 x 15
- EZ bar curls: 3 x 8–10
- Incline DB curls: 3 x 12

Day 5 — Lower B
- Deadlift: 5 x 4–6 (heavier)
- Bulgarian split: 4 x 8–10

Integrated cardio plan (by phase)

Cheat‑meal day guidance

- Calorie bump: +300–800 kcal above normal daily target (monitor results).
- Place cheat meal after a training day or on a rest day to aid recovery; avoid heavy cheat right before a heavy leg day.

Monitoring & adjustment
- Track weights, reps, RIR, bodyweight once/week (same time), and photos/measures every 2–4 weeks.
- If strength/performance drops or soreness accumulates for >2 weeks, reduce cardio, lower accessory volume, or add an extra deload week.
- Modify calories: if no weight gain after 2–3 weeks, add +150–300 kcal/day; if too much fat gain, reduce daily surplus to +150 kcal until stabilized.
- Keep protein at 150 g/day across phases; use protein powder to top up when needed.

Sample progression checklist for trainer to use
- Week‑to‑week: if all working sets hit reps and RPE ≤ target with good form → increase load next week.
- If only some sets hit target reps → keep load, aim for extra rep/set next session.
- If repeated failures → drop load 5% and assess recovery/nutrition.
- Record one main lift PR attempt only when well recovered (prefer Week 11 if testing) with spotters.

Safety & coaching cues
- Emphasize bracing, neutral spine, scapular stability.
- Use spotters for heavy bench and squats; consider safety pins for singles.
- Progress intensity only when technique is solid. Substitute trap bar for conventional deadlift if safer for client.
